clue.text: Failed to bid spades, surprisingly

definitions.note: in bridge a player who declines to bid says 'pass', so this is the past tense of that call

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters of the card suit's name turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A bridge player surprisingly declined to bid in spades.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, choosing not to make a bid is a pass, so a player who failed to bid has done this.

clue.text: Queues for stories like Animal Farm, you could say

indicators.note: you could say signals that the words are to be judged by how they are spoken

parts.note: Orwell's Animal Farm is a fable about farmyard swine, so such books are pig tales

explanation.surface: A list of tales about farm animals, Orwell's included.
explanation.walkthrough: A queue is an old word for a braid of hair hanging behind the head, not a line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Queue is an old name for a plait of hair worn hanging at the back, the same as a braid tied behind.

clue.text: Shopaholic needs us to provide material support

definitions.note: a fabric strap holding up a stocking or sock

indicators.note: the shopaholic needs us inside, so the word is placed within the spender

parts.note: a shopaholic is a compulsive spender

explanation.surface: A compulsive shopper needs our financial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is an elastic strap that holds up stockings, a support made of material.

clue.text: An antelope's short dash

indicators.note: short means the antelope's name loses its final letter

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: An antelope makes a brief sprint.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or verve, the same spirited style that dash describes.

clue.text: Watercolour?

parts.note: read not as a kind of paint but as a picture whose colour is the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A painting of the ocean is a marine picture, quite literally a picture of water.

clue.text: One's letters get harder to read

definitions.text: One's letters get harder to read

parts.words: One's letters get harder to read
parts.note: an optician's test card has rows of letters that shrink line by line

explanation.definitionFit: An optician's test card has letters getting smaller row by row, so they become harder to make out.

clue.text: Thrilled by celebrity, or attacked by one!

definitions.meaning: literally hit by a famous person, a celebrity being a star

explanation.surface: A fan thrilled by a famous person, or one who was assaulted by them.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awed by fame is the everyday sense; the literal one is being hit by a celebrity.

clue.text: First person to uphold a liberal defence

indicators.note: in a down answer the thing upholding sits underneath, so the pronoun goes at the bottom

parts.note: I is the first person singular pronoun

explanation.surface: Someone is first to stand up for a liberal's justification.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a plea in a defence that the accused was somewhere else at the time.

clue.text: Sporting side appearing in Mexico

parts.note: a football or cricket team is often written XI, and those letters sit inside MEXICO

explanation.walkthrough: A team of this size is written XI in Roman numerals, and XI can be seen in the middle of MEXICO.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has this number of players, so the word names such a side.

clue.text: Crazy instruction the young must sit through

definitions.text: Crazy instruction the young must sit through

parts.note: potty is British slang for mad or crazy
training is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: Toddlers must sit through some mad lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A potty is a child's toilet bowl; the toddler literally sits through this teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Teaching toddlers to use a child's toilet is lessons they sit on, quite literally.

clue.text: Men in black exposed in postage fddle

indicators.note: a misprint of 'fiddle', meaning to fiddle with or rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Uniformed men exposed in a stamp-money scam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fddle' is printed for 'fiddle', and the letters of 'postage' are fiddled.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret police were feared figures commonly pictured in dark uniforms and coats.

clue.text: Investigate test in English

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A teacher looks into a test in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to inspect it closely, the same as to look into it.

clue.text: One starts roosting in a maple tree

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

indicators.note: starts picks only the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A bird begins to roost in a maple.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus name of the maples, used for those trees in gardening.

clue.text: Items that I need to reorder right now

indicators.note: to reorder says the three words' letters must be placed in a new sequence

explanation.surface: Some goods I need to order again immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase means at present or currently, the same as immediately now.

clue.text: Where nude models may appear with body piercings

definitions.text: Where nude models may appear with body piercings

parts.words: Where nude models may appear with body piercings
parts.note: the middle pages of a magazine, held together by staples driven through the models' pictures

explanation.walkthrough: The 'body piercings' are the staples through the middle spread of a magazine, which pierce the pictured bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle spread of a magazine, often a nude pin-up, is stapled through its fold.

clue.text: Main concern of young man with odd ideas?

definitions.text: Main concern of young man with odd ideas?

parts.note: a lad is a young man

indicators.note: odd means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: What a young man thinks about most, with his strange notions.
explanation.definitionFit: Women are, the clue jokes, what a young fellow chiefly thinks about.

clue.text: Empty tanker takes on one army corps for Greek warship

indicators.note: empty means the word's inside letters are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A tanker with nothing aboard takes a military unit to fight Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps that repairs vehicles and kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient galley with three banks of oars, used by Greek fleets.

clue.text: Fat horse fed with special grain

indicators.note: fed with puts the second element inside the first, as food goes into an animal

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: special suggests the grain's letters are made into a particular new order

explanation.surface: A plump horse was given special grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' reads as describing the horse, but it is the definition: a spread used like butter. 'special' rearranges the grain, and 'fed with' puts the result (GARIN) in the mare.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a spread made from vegetable oils, a cooking fat used like butter.

clue.text: See 9
Not laid down by Article V, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A rule not set out by the fifth article of a constitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing upright is not lying flat, so it is the opposite of laid down.

clue.text: Bookmakers work in them risk picking the odds

indicators.note: picking the odds means taking the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the run

explanation.surface: Bookies work where there is a risk of taking odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmakers' suggests betting shops; it means people who make books.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors make books, so the clue reads the word for bookies literally as authors.

clue.text: A number of men told to mount up

indicators.note: told means as spoken, so the phrase is judged by how it is heard

parts.note: a crew is a team of men, such as on a ship

explanation.surface: Several men were ordered to get on their horses.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrue is to accumulate or build up gradually, as interest does.

clue.text: Greek island, quiet, with atmosphere — not half!

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: not half means only half of the long word is kept, the first five letters

explanation.surface: A quiet Greek island, not half atmospheric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is also a British exclamation meaning 'absolutely', but here it leaves only the front half of 'atmosphere'.
explanation.definitionFit: Patmos is an island in the Aegean's Dodecanese group, where St John wrote Revelation.

clue.text: School punishment once applied to staff!

definitions.meaning: a staff is a walking pole or cane

explanation.surface: A beating once given to school staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A cane for beating pupils was once used in schools; a staff is a walking pole.

clue.text: Gold prospectors once, doomed to failure

definitions.text: Gold prospectors once, doomed to failure

parts.words: Gold prospectors once, doomed to failure
parts.note: medieval experimenters who tried to make gold from base metals, which can never work

explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners tried to transmute lead into gold, a quest that could never succeed.

clue.text: Queen's favourite company with right sort of soldier

parts.note: a GI is a US Army soldier

explanation.surface: The monarch's favourite firm comes with the correct type of serviceman.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Elizabeth II famously kept many of these small Welsh dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh breed was the late Queen Elizabeth II's best-loved dog, which she kept all her life.

clue.text: Yet it means everything to an actor

definitions.text: Yet it means everything to an actor

parts.words: Yet it means everything to an actor
parts.note: a role is only a portion, yet a performer's career depends on getting one

explanation.definitionFit: A role in a play is a portion, not the whole, yet a performer craves one.

clue.text: Bank of Scotland needs support introducing euro

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
E is a symbol abbreviation for the euro

explanation.surface: A Scottish bank needs backing as it introduces the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Bank of Scotland' is not the bank but a Scottish hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or slope, a bank of earth in Scotland.

clue.text: Polo ponies' centre supplying famous Italian

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller

indicators.note: centre takes the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: The middle of the polo ponies is supplied by a celebrated Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polo' looks like the horse sport but stands for the traveller Marco Polo.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian pioneer of radio, a well-known figure from Italy.

clue.text: Jack possibly needs one on account of his heart

parts.note: a jack is one example of a playing card
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Jack may need someone on account of his heart condition.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective means relating to the heart, so a cardiac problem is one of his heart.

clue.text: Noisy parties in lodgings start off quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
digs is British slang for rented rooms

explanation.surface: Loud parties in rented rooms start with a call for silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start off' puts the call for quiet at the front; DIGS is British slang for lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively, boisterous party or celebration.

clue.text: Happened to be cut down

parts.note: to fell a tree is to cut it down

explanation.surface: A tree happened to be cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Befell means occurred or took place, often of something bad.
